Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Godzilla accounts operate under usage quotas determined by your plan tier. Quotas apply at the workspace level across API request throughput, monthly event volume, and concurrent pipeline resources.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is assigned to a tier that dictates default rate limits and monthly event capacities.

Plan Rate limit Monthly events Active pipelines Support SLA
Starter 100 req / min 50,000 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req / min 1,000,000 25 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+ req / min) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated SLA

What happens when you exceed a quota

Exceeding limits is handled differently depending on whether you exceed a per-minute API request rate or a monthly event volume quota.

API rate limits (HTTP 429)

If your application sends more requests in a one-minute window than your tier allows, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before resuming requests. See Limits, quotas & errors for header details and retry strategies.

Monthly event quotas

Monthly event usage resets on the first day of your billing cycle. When approaching or exceeding event limits:

  • 80% and 100% threshold alerts: Account admins receive email notifications and webhook lifecycle events (workspace.quota_warning) when approaching your limit.
  • Standard plan overages: On the Standard tier, pipelines continue running without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.15 per 10,000 events on your next invoice.
  • Starter plan cap: Starter tier workspaces pause pipeline ingestion once the 50,000 event limit is reached until the next billing cycle or an upgrade to Standard.

Resource limits (pipelines and connectors)

If you attempt to create more active pipelines or connectors than your plan allows, the API returns a 403 Forbidden with code quota_exceeded.

Upgrading and quota increases

You can upgrade your plan or add billing details directly from workspace settings. If your workload requires higher burst rate limits or tailored enterprise terms, reach out via Troubleshooting / FAQ.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Monitoring usage|body_html=

Check your current monthly event consumption and active pipeline counts anytime in the workspace dashboard or via the workspace metadata endpoint.

Migration guide (v1 → v2) {{ds:component/chip|label=v1 retired|variant=danger}}

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Limits, quotas & errors for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

Godzilla is built from core concepts that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/0881cc13-706b-45dc-b215-08b706dc8fdb}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/3cc1aa67-f674-447d-8dda-ac55a42c26eb}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/aaba4e33-be69-4693-8066-1c2f622b674b}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/88ecedb3-543b-4dcf-b985-6fb94e4eaa95}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=Declarative contracts that define and validate the structure of event payloads flowing through pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, validates their schemas, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Limits, quotas & errors.
Quota
Usage allowances assigned to a workspace based on its plan tier, covering request throughput and monthly event volume. See Quotas & billing.

args.body:
Migration guide (v1 → v2) {{ds:component/chip|label=v1 retired|variant=danger}}

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Rate limits for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

}}

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

args.body:
Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Godzilla accounts operate under usage quotas determined by your plan tier. Quotas apply at the workspace level across API request throughput, monthly event volume, and concurrent pipeline resources.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is assigned to a tier that dictates default rate limits and monthly event capacities.

Plan Rate limit Monthly events Active pipelines Support SLA
Starter 100 req / min 50,000 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req / min 1,000,000 25 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+ req / min) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated SLA

What happens when you exceed a quota

Exceeding limits is handled differently depending on whether you exceed a per-minute API request rate or a monthly event volume quota.

API rate limits (HTTP 429)

If your application sends more requests in a one-minute window than your tier allows, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before resuming requests. See Rate limits for header details and retry strategies.

Monthly event quotas

Monthly event usage resets on the first day of your billing cycle. When approaching or exceeding event limits:

  • 80% and 100% threshold alerts: Account admins receive email notifications and webhook lifecycle events (workspace.quota_warning) when approaching your limit.
  • Standard plan overages: On the Standard tier, pipelines continue running without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.15 per 10,000 events on your next invoice.
  • Starter plan cap: Starter tier workspaces pause pipeline ingestion once the 50,000 event limit is reached until the next billing cycle or an upgrade to Standard.

Resource limits (pipelines and connectors)

If you attempt to create more active pipelines or connectors than your plan allows, the API returns a 403 Forbidden with code quota_exceeded.

Upgrading and quota increases

You can upgrade your plan or add billing details directly from workspace settings. If your workload requires higher burst rate limits or tailored enterprise terms, reach out via Troubleshooting / FAQ.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Monitoring usage|body_html=

Check your current monthly event consumption and active pipeline counts anytime in the workspace dashboard or via the workspace metadata endpoint.

}} {{ds:component/docs-toc|items_html=

  • What happens when you exceed a quota
  • Upgrading and quota increases

args.body:
Troubleshooting / FAQ

Common problems, and where in the docs to go for the full explanation.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

Walk through Error handling & recovery — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

Verify your endpoint returns a 2xx status and that you're checking X-Godzilla-Signature correctly — a rejected signature looks identical to a dropped delivery from the outside. Full details in the Webhooks endpoint reference.

I'm getting 429s

You've hit the standard-tier limit described in Rate limits. Back off using the Retry-After header, or review Quotas & billing to learn about plan tiers and how overages are handled.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Migrating from v1?|body_html=

A number of "it worked yesterday" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.

}}

Contact channels

  • Technical support: support@godzilladocs.dev
  • Sales: sales@godzilladocs.dev
  • Security reports: security@godzilladocs.dev — see Security & compliance overview for our disclosure policy.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Response times|body_html=

Standard-tier support responds within one business day. Include your workspace ID and, if relevant, a request_id from an error response.

}}

Godzilla is built from core concepts that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/0881cc13-706b-45dc-b215-08b706dc8fdb}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/3cc1aa67-f674-447d-8dda-ac55a42c26eb}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/aaba4e33-be69-4693-8066-1c2f622b674b}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/88ecedb3-543b-4dcf-b985-6fb94e4eaa95}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=Declarative contracts that define and validate the structure of event payloads flowing through pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, validates their schemas, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits.
Quota
Usage allowances assigned to a workspace based on its plan tier, covering request throughput and monthly event volume. See Quotas & billing.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

Authentication

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

Getting an API key

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits.

Using the key

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}

Verifying webhook requests

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.
